items.title: Pending order Desk Lamp variant change and refund

items.body:
Prior task outcome: success.

Observed: The agent authenticated the customer using name and ZIP after the customer said they did not remember their email, looked up order #W9300146, and found it pending with one Desk Lamp. Product details identified the cheapest available variant as black, medium brightness, AC adapter for $135.24, compared with the original price of $153.23. Before making the change, the agent disclosed the variant, $17.99 refund to the original gift card, and that the once-only item change would prevent further modification or cancellation, then asked for explicit confirmation. After the customer agreed, the modification tool returned the replacement item and a $17.98999999999998 gift-card refund; the agent confirmed it as $17.99.

Evidence-supported lesson: For a pending-order item change, verify the order and variant availability/prices, explain the exact change and consequential one-time limitation, gather all intended changes, and obtain explicit confirmation before updating. The observed operation changed only one item and used the existing gift card for the price difference. This evidence supports the described scenario, not every store workflow; the conversation does not establish broader procedures.
items.title: Pending order item modification with explicit confirmation

target_cues.37: Look for evidence that item changes depend on the current order status and the requested replacement. An earlier order ID, item, price or approval belongs to the donor.
